chapter_title: Chapter 8, note 16.
text: An adequate theory of Judaism must ultimately attempt to develop a perspective on the origins of Judaism as a group evolutionary strategy.

chapter_title: Chapter 8, note 16.
text: Clearly, one source of the fascination that Judaism has presented over the centuries to intellectuals has been the uniqueness of Judaism and its persistence in its uniqueness over very long periods of historical time.

Clearly, one source 
of the fascination that Judaism has presented over the centuries to intellectuals

chapter_title: Chapter 8, note 16.
text: In attempting to develop a theoretical perspective on this question, it is important to remember the general theoretical perspective developed in Chapter 1.
text_raw:
In attempting to develop a theoretical 
perspective on this question, it is important to remember the general theoretical

chapter_title: Chapter 8, note 16.
text: The theoretical perspective developed there specifically allows for “cultural” influences on evolutionary strategies.
text_raw:
The theoretical perspective developed there specifically allows for “cultural” 
influences on evolutionary strategies.

chapter_title: Chapter 8, note 16.
text: Humans are viewed as “flexible strategizers” (Alexander 1987) who are able to develop ideologies and social systems that are intended to further evolutionary ends.
text_raw:
Humans are viewed as “flexible 
strategizers” (Alexander 1987) who are able to develop ideologies and social 
systems that are intended to further evolutionary ends.

chapter_title: Chapter 8, note 16.
text: These evolutionary goals are assumed to have a powerful genetic component, but the means by which one attains these evolutionary goals can utilize higher-level (“domain-general”) cognitive processes and be influenced by experience.
text_raw:
These evolutionary goals 
are assumed to have a powerful genetic component, but the means by which one 
attains these evolutionary goals can utilize higher-level (“domain-general”) 
cognitive processes and be influenced by experience.

chapter_title: Chapter 8, note 16.
text: In the same way that their cognitive capabilities enable hum ans to make inventions or learn new methods of warfare, the present perspective is highly compatible with the idea that an evolutionary strategy could be contrive d on the basis of specific experiences or on the basis of a general understanding or theory of human nature.
text_raw:
In the same way that their 
cognitive capabilities enable hum ans to make inventions or learn new methods 
of warfare, the present perspective is highly compatible with the idea that an 
evolutionary strategy could be contrive d on the basis of specific experiences or 
on the basis of a general understanding or theory of human nature.

chapter_title: Chapter 8, note 16.
text: However, in Chapter 1, it was mentioned that genetic and environmental variation in psychological mechanisms may also be important to the development of group evolutionary strategies.
text_raw:

variation in psychological mechanisms may also be important to the

chapter_title: Chapter 8, note 16.
text: If indeed the type of group evolutionary strategy represented by Judaism “pulls” for certain psychological predispositions, then it is reasonable to suppose that there may be biological predispositions for engaging in the type of group evolutionary strategy represented by Judaism.
